transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-28 14:30 UTC
Duration: 52 mins
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marco (Redwood CSM), Dana (Galaxy SRE), Kenji (Galaxy Platform), Leah (Galaxy Product Ops), Omar (Galaxy Security)

Summary notes (auto-generated, may be incomplete): Quick postmortem follow-up after the April 22 degradation. Focus on containment measures already applied and a path to prevent recurrence via autoscale tuning, cache eviction logic, and improved telemetry.

[00:00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for squeezing this in. can we do a quick round trip on the april incident and the mitigations y'all already have in place?
[00:00:12] Dana: yeah thanks alex. i'll start, quick recap — on april 22 we saw a multi-tenant burst, token rates spiked, our prefix cache warmed odd and then free'd, which caused higher compute tail latency and a cascade of queued requests. the autoscaler k-shed didn't keep up.
[00:00:29] Priya: sorry, k-shed? do you mean the k8s horizontal autoscaler or your custom shedder?
[00:00:33] Dana: oh yeah that was shorthand — our hpa plus a preemption script we run in the autoscaler loop. it triggered late.
[00:00:40] Kenji: and to add, the KV cache eviction was tuned for memory headroom, but the eviction policy kicked out larger prefixes first which are actually the cache hot-path for your evaluation workload. so we lost a lot of kv state.
[00:00:52] Priya: got it. that matches what we saw in our traces — big k-v cache misses correlated with token re-computation spikes. we logged long tail p95/p99 increases.
[00:01:02] Marco: for context we also saw increased retries from the application layer which amplified request fanout. not ideal.
[00:01:08] Leah: customer impact was mostly background embedding jobs slowed, but a handful of real-time inference calls hit timeouts. ops paged us.
[00:01:16] Omar: quick security note — any changes to cache persistence or failover must be logged for audit purpose. we need evidence for the SOC2 lane.
[00:01:23] Alex: understood. let's walk through what Redwood recommended and what's been applied. priya, can you summarize the short-term patches?
[00:01:29] Priya: sure. immediate fixes: 1) disabled aggressive eviction for prefix-sized entries, changed to lru-stable policy; 2) lowered preemption threshold in autoscaler so we scale earlier for sustained token-rate spikes; 3) added a circuit-breaker on application retry loops to prevent fanout amplification. these were staged last week and rolled to canary, then to 60% of traffic.
[00:01:54] Dana: we saw i guess a 30 to 40% reduction in the worst of the p99 after the canary. not perfect, but better.
[00:02:01] Priya: yeah the numbers look promising. we still need to validate at peak synthetic load.
[00:02:07] Kenji: our question — what's the recommended autoscaler target for redwood dedicated when handling spiky inference workloads? current target is 60% GPU util, but we think that's too high for bursty.
[00:02:18] Priya: for bursty workloads we usually recommend a lower target, 40–50% GPU util, combined with a short ramp period. also turn on predictive scaling if you can feed the traffic estimator.
[00:02:28] Marco: we can share the autoscaler config we've onboarded — alex will attach it after this call.
[00:02:33] Alex: yep will do.
[00:02:35] [00:02:35] Dana: one open point — the KV cache corruption alert we had during the spike, it looked transient, but we want a definitive root cause. our team still sees occasional checksum mismatches in the cache store.
[00:02:47] Priya: i remember that — that lined up with rapid eviction and rehydration under contention. sometimes rehydration overlaps and we saw partial writes. we added a small lock window to rehydrate and made writes idempotent.
[00:02:59] Kenji: is there a risk that the lock window will add latency?
[00:03:03] Priya: small risk — we keep the lock at sub-5ms in normal conditions; the alternative was repeated rehydration causing repeated compute. tradeoff favored the lock.
[00:03:11] Leah: timeline questions — when can we expect the full RCA doc?
[00:03:15] Marco: we committed to a draft by end of this week; full RCA with mitigations and timeline by next Tuesday.
[00:03:21] Dana: can you include the flamegraphs and the request-id correlation we asked for?
[00:03:24] Marco: yep — flamegraphs + raw traces attached.
[00:03:29] [00:03:29] Omar: security again — if we're changing cache persistence, we need to run through the data retention matrix. even ephemeral cache writes might contain hashed customer identifiers. we can't assume they're harmless.
[00:03:40] Priya: totally. our recommended approach is to keep prefix cache in encrypted ephemeral volumes and rotate keys per week; Redwood can provide the KMS integration notes.
[00:03:49] Omar: good — send the KMS integration doc. also need a list of logs and fields that'll be stored for auditing.
[00:03:56] Alex: i'll attach the KMS integration and the redact/PII guidance after the call.
[00:03:59] [00:03:59] Dana: operationally we want to avoid full eviction during spikes. is there a way for Redwood to dynamically bias cache eviction based on recent heat maps?
[00:04:10] Priya: yes — Redwood supports heat-aware eviction tiers; that feature's in our optimize toolkit. you can set thresholds to protect hot-prefixes for up to X minutes after last access. we can propose a conservative profile for your workload.
[00:04:22] Kenji: can you quantify X? like 2 minutes? 10?
[00:04:25] Priya: defaults are 5 minutes but configurable. for your workload i'd start with 8 minutes to reduce churn.
[00:04:30] Leah: how do we measure improvement? what dashboards should we watch?
[00:04:33] Priya: key metrics: prefix eviction rate, cache hit ratio, p95/p99 server latency, queue length and scale-up events. we'll send a sample dashboard.
[00:04:41] Marco: also add cost telemetry — lower eviction might increase GPU ops, so show cost delta and latency trade-off.
[00:04:47] [00:04:47] Dana: on the canary plan — we want a very short window for canary validation. what are the success criteria you'd use?
[00:04:53] Priya: success criteria: no more than 10% increase in p95, at least 25% reduction in eviction spikes during the verification window, and no retry amplifications beyond baseline. also no new errors.
[00:05:04] Dana: ok makes sense. we'll map that to our SLOs and decide.
  
[00:05:10] Kenji: about runbooks — our ops folks found the previous runbook a bit hand-wavy. can we co-author a deterministic checklist for the next 6 months?
[00:05:18] Marco: yes — we're proposing a 2-part runbook: immediate containment (circuit breakers, scale-up policy) and post-containment diagnostics (trace extraction, cache verification). we'd like Galaxy to own the first responder tasks and Redwood to own deeper traces and remediation code snippets.
[00:05:34] Leah: timeline for co-authoring?
[00:05:36] Marco: draft in 5 business days.
[00:05:39] [00:05:39] Alex: switching to long-term items — autoscale predictive model, improved backpressure policies, and a fallback routing to a smaller-latency model in case of sustained overloads.
[00:05:50] Priya: fallback routing is interesting — we can configure route policies so that traffic degrades to a cheaper, lower-latency quantized model when latency exceeds threshold. that preserves availability.
[00:06:00] Dana: do we lose quality? yes, but it's an acceptable graceful degradation — better than timeouts.
[00:06:05] Kenji: what's the typical cost delta for keeping both replicas warmed?
[00:06:09] Priya: depends on model sizes — ballpark extra 15–25% compute cost to maintain warmed fallback instances. we'll provide an estimate for your model catalog.
[00:06:18] Omar: also need to log which model served the request for audit — so we can show fallback usage per customer.
[00:06:23] Priya: we'll include model_id logging and tags in the telemetry.
[00:06:27] [00:06:27] Dana: on alerts — thresholds felt too sensitive pre-spike, so we silenced a lot. we want better signal to reduce alert noise but still catch the early escalations.
[00:06:36] Marco: recommended: move to composite alerts that require two signals (e.g., eviction rate spike + queue length growth) to avoid false positives. set a 3-minute evaluation window to tolerate transients.
[00:06:48] Leah: who owns tuning those alert rules?
[00:06:50] Alex: Redwood Obs team can propose rule changes; Galaxy SRE will approve and push through.
[00:06:56] [00:06:56] Dana: small thing — we noticed Tokenization differences between our test harness and prod which affects request sizes; any guidance?
[00:07:03] Priya: ensure you use the same tokenizer version and BPE merge tables we vetted. mismatched tokenization can change seqlength distributions substantially. we've seen 8–12% longer sequences in mismatched setups.
[00:07:14] Kenji: we'll reconcile and run a synthetic load that mirrors prod token distribution.
[00:07:19] [00:07:19] Marco: quick operational ask — can Redwood run a 2-hour soak at projected peak next Tuesday? we could join and watch the metrics live.
[00:07:27] Alex: yes, we can coordinate. Priya will schedule with your ops team.
[00:07:31] Priya: i'll propose time slots post-call.
[00:07:34] [00:07:34] Omar: last security item — retention of debug logs: we need to redact any PII before logs leave the VPC. is Redwood fine with on-host redaction hooks?
[00:07:43] Priya: yes, Redwood supports ingestion-time redaction. we'll send the redaction config and schema.
[00:07:49] Dana: great.
[00:07:51] [00:07:51] Leah: okay to recap next steps?
[00:07:54] Alex: recap: Redwood to share autoscaler config, canary runbook, KMS integration notes, and proposed dashboards. Galaxy to provide flamegraphs, traffic slices, and approve pilot schedule. both to co-author runbook draft. follow-up call week of June 21.
[00:08:11] Marco: i'll put calendar invites and attach the initial documents.
[00:08:16] [00:08:16] Priya: any outstanding questions?
[00:08:18] Dana: none from me. thanks all.
[00:08:21] Kenji: thanks.
[00:08:23] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with artifacts.

Transcript end. Note: transcription includes some speaker shorthand and may mis-attribute short interjections.
